question: Which of the following types of materials is NOT used in an oil filter as a strainer?
solution:
The correct answer is __Thin aluminum foil**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Oil filters__ are designed to remove contaminants from engine oil, transmission oil, or hydraulic oil.
 
• They use various materials as strainers, such as wire screens, felt, and cloth, to trap impurities.
 
• Thin aluminum foil is not used in oil filters due to its lack of porosity and structural integrity.
 
• Using inappropriate materials like aluminum foil can lead to engine damage and reduced efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Wire Screen:**

 
 
• Wire screens are commonly used in oil filters for their durability and ability to trap particles.
 
• They are generally made from stainless steel or other robust materials.
 
 
 
• **Felt:**
 
 
• Felt is a fibrous material used in some oil filters to trap very fine particles.
 
• It is known for its high absorbency and filtration efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Cloth:**
 
 
• Cloth-based filters are used in some applications for additional filtration support and trapping small particles.
